text:
Predicates:
Likes(x, y) ::: x likes y.
Barks(y) ::: y barks.
Dog(y) ::: y is a dog.
Animal(y) ::: y is an animal.
Jumps(y) ::: y jumps.
HasLegs(y) ::: y has legs.
Terricolous(y) ::: y is terricolous.
Premises:
∀y ((Animal(y) ∧ Barks(y)) → ¬Likes(jane, y)) ::: Jane does not like any animals that bark.
∀y (Dog(y) → (Animal(y) ∧ Barks(y))) ::: All dogs are animals that bark.
∀y ((Animal(y) ∧ Jumps(y)) → Likes(jane, y)) ::: Jane likes all animals that jump.
∀y (Animal(y) → (HasLegs(y) → Jumps(y))) ::: If an animal has legs, then it jumps.
∀y (Animal(y) → (Terricolous(y) → HasLegs(y))) ::: If an animal is terricolous, then it has legs.
Animal(kiki) ::: KiKi is an animal.
¬(Jumps(kiki) ∨ HasLegs(kiki)) → (Terricolous(kiki) ∨ HasLegs(kiki)) ::: If KiKi neither jumps nor has legs, then KiKi is terricolous or has legs.
Conclusion:
Dog(kiki) ∧ Barks(kiki) ::: KiKi is a barking dog.
